why: The answer says that int c; gives c the value 0, but a local variable has no value until it is assigned. That rule is wrong in Java, so the answer is L0: println(c + 1) does not compile.

concepts.quote: int c; declares c, so c is 0.
concepts.why: It uses the wrong rule that a local variable gets a default value of 0; in Java, reading c before it is assigned is a compile error.
It treats c as already holding a value, but a variable must be assigned before it is read, so c + 1 is rejected by the compiler.
The answer says nothing about int's range or its arithmetic, only about the declaration, so there is nothing to mark for int.
The answer does not mention double.
